kanban-claude 0.2.0.dev8

The web board is gone, workers run in a smaller sandbox with spending caps, and the owner can watch the board with one command that exits only when something needs them. This page explains what changed and why.

Release explainer, 2026-10-20. Diff d1a40cf (main) to aff1750 (feature/modernization). Dev pre-release.

  • 48

    commits between main and the branch head

  • 72

    files changed

  • +4,552 / −3,730

    lines added and removed (git diff --shortstat d1a40cf aff1750)

  • 4→5

    database schema version; the upgrade backs up the old file first

Background

What kanban-claude is, and why dev8 exists

kanban-claude is a daemon that runs on the owner's Mac. It keeps a board of cards and starts Claude Code agents on them, one role per card. Smith and designer build and open pull requests, warden reviews them, and scout works under a narrower write allowance (it may not use Edit). The owner talks to the board through the kanban CLI and the orchestrator skill.

dev8 is the release of the feature/modernization branch. The CHANGELOG sorts it into one removal (the web board), a long list of additions, a set of behaviour changes and three fixes. Read together, the changes fall into four groups: the owner's view of the board moves to the CLI and the pane; workers are isolated and capped; merging and CI waits get explicit states; scheduling and housekeeping close a few gaps.

The reasons come from commit messages, the CHANGELOG and the modernization plan (plugins/kanban-claude/docs/modernization-plan.md). The plan's items are cited by id (P0-1 to P3-4, each with Evidence, Source and Fix) and its decisions as D1 to D12.

Line numbers below are in plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/ at 9ff5306, the head before the pane merge, unless a path says otherwise.

Walkthrough

Area by area

Each area says what changed, why, and how you notice it as the operator.

The web board is removed −removed

What changed
web.py, its three asset files (1,772 lines together) and test_web.py (1,137 lines) are deleted. The daemon now runs three threads: tick, notify and housekeeping (daemon.py:170-171). Also gone: the board verb, setup --port, the config keys web.port and web.jira_base_url, the web.secret mode check in doctor, and the o hotkey in the pane that opened the board (hooks/board.tsx).
Why
The plan lists three UIs (P3-2): the CLI, web.py with 922 lines of assets (1,772 lines together), and the 212-line hooks/board.tsx pane. No usage data existed for either visual UI. Decision D4 recommended dropping the web board and keeping the pane, which lives where the owner already works. Commit f22385d records the choice: “Denis chose the CLI and the board.tsx mod over web.py (D4)”. The risk D4 names: the pane depends on Claude Code's mod API.
How you notice it
kanban board is an unknown verb. config list shows no web.* keys, and a leftover web.port row is ignored because config list and get only walk the defaults. setup ends with “kanban-claude X is set up.” and no URL. A web.secret file in $KANBAN_HOME is no longer read and can be deleted. Your views are now list, show, digest, watch --actionable and the /kanban-board pane.

Workers are isolated from the owner's setup +added~changed

What changed
runner.py builds each run's environment. plugins_off (:97) switches off every plugin the account enables, except kanban-claude, its dependency frontend-design and worker.plugin_allowlist; it always disables cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin. mcp_config (:127) copies MCP servers from the account's .claude.json into a private 0600 file next to the run log (suffix .mcp.json), removed when the run ends (:341). A repo .mcp.json only supplies names the account lacks. The argv gets --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config. worker.mcp_allowlist defaults to context7, lightpanda, code-review-graph (store.py:205). role_denies (:106) and settings_json (:115) pass per-role denies with --settings: Agent(x) is denied for every agent except the role's helper (card-helper for smith, designer and scout; review-helper for warden); Edit and Write are denied for warden and atlassian; Edit is denied for scout. Each card gets its own TMPDIR at $KANBAN_WORK/tmp/<card> (paths.card_tmp, paths.py:64). GH_HOST is set only when the origin host is not github.com and the card is not scratch (origin_host, :185).
Why
Plan P2-1: the owner's ponytail and benjamin hooks and user MCPs loaded into every worker, and the designer started with 289K tokens of cache read against 28K for smith. The fix disables every user plugin except kanban-claude and an allowlist, and passes a strict MCP config. D9 sets the default: workers get no vault and no user MCPs, and a board can allowlist one in config. D1 chose per-role denies in the runner (Edit and Write for warden, scout and atlassian, and Agent(...) beyond the helper) instead of a tools: exemption in tests/plugins/verify.py. The shared temp dir is plan P0-1: all workers inherited the daemon's TMPDIR, so PR bodies were swapped between cards (about 22 sessions). The temp dir sits outside KANBAN_HOME because the Edit(KANBAN_HOME/**) deny also blocks the Write tool (commit 316bcc3). GH_HOST is plan P0-8: on GHE repos gh in a worker went to github.com.
How you notice it
A worker no longer sees your personal plugins or MCP servers. If a role needs one, add its name to worker.plugin_allowlist or worker.mcp_allowlist. While a run is live, a 0600 .mcp.json sits beside its log.

Budget caps and effort per role +added~changed✓fixed

What changed
store._over_budget (:1503) runs inside claim (:1541). budget.max_usd_per_card defaults to 15.0; budget.max_usd_per_board_day is off by default; 0 turns a check off; the day is the local day. A card over a cap is blocked with block_kind capability and a comment that starts “BLOCKED:” and names the key and the fix. The older budget.max_usd_per_run (30) and budget.ceiling (100) are unchanged. Effort (model_effort, :75) resolves from the card (non-review runs), then effort.<role>, then effort.default (xhigh). Review runs use effort.<role> or effort.review (high) and ignore the card's effort. effort.scout still defaults to high; smith, designer, warden and atlassian default to none. config set now validates effort.* and models.* (commit 74a8492). The effort: line is removed from the atlassian, designer, scout, smith and warden agent files; card-checker keeps medium.
Why
Plan P2-4: the per-run cap of 30 USD never binds (the largest run cost 7.69 USD), and nothing capped a card or a board; per card the median was 2.28 USD, p90 6.32 USD, max 11.93 USD. D8 turned the card cap on at 15 USD, above the observed maximum, and left the board-day cap off until set (Denis mentioned 75 USD). Effort is plan P0-11: --effort from model_effort always overrode the agent frontmatter, so effort: was dead for dispatched roles (atlassian declared medium and ran at xhigh). The fix removes it from the five dispatched roles so one place decides; card-checker, card-helper and review-helper are not dispatched and keep theirs. D11 leaves effort.default at xhigh until an A/B of xhigh against high. Commit 74a8492: a typo such as effort.smith turbo used to make every run fail. Commit bd7a059: before the fix, a card blocked at a review claim unblocked to ready with warden assigned, so it ran as a work run and went to done with no review (blocked_in_review, :1108).
How you notice it
A blocked card carries a comment such as “BLOCKED: ...” with kanban config set <key> <usd> and kanban unblock <id> --reason "cap raised". The event payload carries from: source. The cap is checked at claim only; a run already going is not stopped by it. A card that is already over 15 USD blocks at its next claim.

Watching the board: actionable events, notify, digest +added~changed

What changed
watch --actionable (cli.py:494) keeps the events in store.ACTIONABLE_EVENTS (:468): blocked, block_loop_detected, gave_up, merge_failed, awaiting_owner_merge, account_paused, quota_wall, dispatch_paused. store.actionable drops events whose actor starts with owner:. It conflicts with --kinds (a usage error). --wait (:520) polls like --follow and exits 0 once at least one line was printed; lines hidden by --actionable do not count. views.watch_line (:76) now ends with the actor, for example (worker:smith#3). The daemon's notify thread (notify_new, daemon.py:105) polls every 5 s. On its first pass it sets the cursor to the current highest event id, and it writes the cursor before it sends. send (:134) uses no shell, a 10 s timeout (NOTIFY_TIMEOUT_S, :26), discards stdout and stderr, and logs a warning on failure. notify.command takes an argv list or a command line, and gets the event line on stdin. kanban digest (views.digest :419; --since defaults to 2h) opens with what needs the owner, then merged, in review, running and cost. kanban followups (default 24h) lists FOLLOW-UP: comments. VERB_HELP (cli.py:73) gives every verb a one-line help.
Why
Plan P1-4: about 80 % of roughly 3,500 events were routine and only about 60 (1.7 %) needed the owner. The Monitor watch, capped at 30 minutes by the harness, was re-armed about 60 times in one slice with more than 150 “nothing to act on” turns, and each expiry woke the session just to re-arm it. The owner's own actions echoed back, and watch lines showed the card's assignee, not who acted. The fix defines the actionable kinds once in the CLI, prints the actor, and adds an optional notify.command for when no session is watching. P1-7: digest answers Denis's question “summarize the last 2 hours, do I need to do something?”. P1-11: follow-ups from warden ledgers were copied by hand into morning.md, so a FOLLOW-UP: prefix and a followups verb list them; no cards are created automatically. P3-4: kanban --help listed no verbs.
How you notice it
A background watch command returns when something needs you. With notify.command set, new actionable events reach your script or notifier; a restart replays nothing, and a command that fails or times out is logged and not retried. kanban doctor check 2 is now daemon_lock (doctor.py:123).

Waiting for CI: wait-ci and transient retry +added✓fixed

What changed
worker.py gains the worker verb wait-ci [--pr N] (wait_ci, :134). It waits up to 540 s (BUDGET_S, :28), polling every 20 s. Exit codes (CI_EXIT, :30): passed 0, failed 1, pending 2; 4 when there is no single open PR (Refused); 5 when the owner runs it (NotAllowed). A failed PR lookup counts as pending, not failed. When a PR reports no checks, _runs (:103) falls back to the workflow runs of the head commit. store.block (:1814) takes retry_after_s: it ends the run with a transient_retry event, counted as a failed run, and sets retry_after to now plus the delay. --retry-after (30m, 2h, 90s or seconds) is allowed with --kind transient only. The agent text says: run wait-ci at most three times; after a third exit 2 with “no checks reported yet”, treat CI as passed and write “no CI checks reported”; if checks are still running, run kanban block --kind transient --retry-after 30m.
Why
Commit 6174d3c: claude moves a Bash call to the background after its 120 s default, which would cut off wait-ci. The runner therefore sets BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 (runner.py:178).
How you notice it
Smith and designer run kanban wait-ci to wait for checks, and its exit code decides their next step. A card blocked with --retry-after returns to the queue by itself. The failure limit (dispatch.failure_limit, default 2) still ends the retries as gave_up, so the card then shows in watch --actionable.

Merging: owner merge, closed PRs, landed content +added~changed✓fixed

What changed
Merge method is per card: --merge-method squash|merge|rebase (a CHECK constraint; ghops.merge takes it, ghops.py:81). A warden approval whose summary contains the partial-review marker (store.complete, :1883) into a feature base sets owner_merge=1, keeps merge_state pending so child cards wait, clears merge_next_at and emits awaiting_owner_merge with partial: True. run_due skips owner_merge rows; settle_owner_merges (housekeeping.py:194) settles the card when the PR is merged. closed_unmerged (:220) turns a PR closed without merge into merge_state='failed' with a merge_failed event, reason pr_closed. When a merge fails but the PR is merged, or the approved head content is already on origin/base (gitops.content_landed, gitops.py:74; used at housekeeping.py:156), the card settles as merged with a landed payload and a comment to close the PR by hand. promote --ignore-merge now stays on the card until reopen, hold or link clears it. reopen, reopen_review, merge_retry and hold reset owner_merge.
Why
Plan P0-5: two merge_failed approval_not_clean events on PR #152. The warden is told to write PARTIAL REVIEW, but the daemon treated it as a broken approval and told the owner to run reopen-review, which re-ran a review that was correct. D10: no auto-merge for a partial review; the card goes to the owner. Its children must keep waiting, which the code does by keeping merge_state pending and setting the new owner_merge column. P0-3: two GHE merge_failed events (cards c17 and c23) where the content had landed but the PR stayed open; the retries pushed empty squash commits and merge_state=failed held back the children. P0-4: four claim_rejected parents_not_done events, because --ignore-merge was kept only in an event payload and not as a column. D2: squash stays the default; a per-card merge_method lets base-sync PRs use a merge commit so their history survives, and merges into main stay owner-only. Commit cb23f9a: before the fix, a PR the owner closed without merging left the card waiting forever and holding its children.
How you notice it
A partial-review card shows as awaiting your merge in list (the awaiting filter includes owner_merge=1 with a pending merge). Merge it on GitHub; the sweep then releases the children. A closed PR shows as merge_failed in watch --actionable.

Migration 5, daemon.lock and the upgrade wait +added~changed

What changed
store.MODERNIZE_SCHEMA (:140) adds tasks.ignore_merge, owner_merge, touches and merge_method. store.migrate takes a backup first, at $KANBAN_HOME/backups/kanban-s<version>-<timestamp>-<hex>.db, and keeps five (BACKUPS_KEPT); a dev7 database is schema 4, so the file is kanban-s4-.... daemon.take_lock (daemon.py:30) writes {"pid", "version"} into daemon.lock. daemon.probe (:48) reads it under a shared non-blocking flock: None means no daemon, an empty dict means the lock is held but nothing is written yet. install.HEALTH_WAIT_S is 30 s (was 10). wait_for_daemon(version) (install.py:297) is called by upgrade with the new version (:426).
Why
Commit b48b71f: after launchctl kickstart the old daemon can still hold the lock, so the wait has to see the new version, not just a live daemon. A dev7 daemon writes no version, so it reads as old.
How you notice it
setup fails with “nothing holds ... after 30 s: the daemon did not start” or “the daemon still runs <ver>, not <ver>, after 30 s”. A new backups/ file appears in $KANBAN_HOME after the first upgrade.

request-review finds the PR itself ~changed

What changed
ghops.pr_list (ghops.py:54) runs gh pr list --head --base --state open. worker._find_pr (:68) refuses zero or several open PRs and prints the fix. The summary now only has to say what the PR changes and how it was checked. The refusal is exit 4.
Why
Plan P0-6: about 5 LPS worker sessions were refused with exit 4 “PR #n is MERGED, not OPEN”, because the summary named an earlier PR first and request-review took the first number in it. GitHub allows one open PR per head and base, so a lookup by the card's branch and base is unique.
How you notice it
A request-review from a branch with no open PR, or with two, fails with a message that says what to do. Summaries no longer carry a PR number.

Scheduling: touches, worktree base, skip reasons +added~changed

What changed
--touches GLOB on create, specify and edit lets two cards in one repo avoid each other. dispatcher.touches_overlap (:139) and overlapping (:154) hold a card back with the skip reason overlaps:<id> (:219). A card without touches is unknown: it never waits and never makes others wait. Review runs are exempt. The code carries a shortcut: note: two wildcard globs on both sides are missed. A scratch card with --branch is refused. A worktree card with no --base and exactly one same-repo worktree parent takes that parent's base (store.create, around :871). list and show print “not started: <reason> (since ...)”. stats now includes accounts.
Why
Plan P1-2: the orchestrator checked file overlap by hand (gh pr list --json files, 12 or more times) and moved doc edits into about 11 separate doc-sweep PRs, because the dispatcher had no overlap check. touches is an optional field the card checker fills from the card's file list; cards without it are unaffected. P1-5: skipped previous_run_alive fires on every review request and the orchestrator kept asking why a card was not running. P1-9: three dev7 cards were created as scratch with --branch, hit a capability block and then provision_failed, and three integration cards were created without --base.
How you notice it
kanban show on a waiting card names the reason. The orchestrator skill now fills --touches from the card-checker output.

Sweep removes TMPDIRs of archived cards ✓fixed

What changed
housekeeping.sweep (:239) removes every $KANBAN_WORK/tmp/<id> whose card is archived or gone. Its docstring says a done card keeps its temp dir so a resumed run can use it.
Why
Plan P0-1 gave each card its own TMPDIR and said to remove it in cleanup_card and in the sweep. The two removals run at different times on purpose. The sweep removes the dir of an archived or deleted card and leaves a done card's alone, because a done card can still be resumed. cleanup_card removes it together with the worktree, when nothing can resume there any more.
How you notice it
The tree under $KANBAN_WORK/tmp shrinks as cards are archived. A done card's dir stays until its worktree is cleaned up (cleanup_card, housekeeping.py:173).

Paused logins are re-probed +added~changed

What changed
dispatcher.reprobe_logins (:98) retries a paused login after 5, 15, then 60 minutes (PROBE_BACKOFF_S). It is called from housekeeping.run_due because the probe can run claude for up to 120 s. The account_paused event now carries task, error and login. A successful probe lifts the pause with an account_resumed event.
Why
Plan P0-9: three auth_lost runs (“Not logged in · Please run /login”) paused the board and it stayed paused until the owner noticed. The account_paused event carried only the config dir, with no card, error or login command, and the pause cleared only through kanban resume. The fix puts the error, the card and the login command into the event, and re-probes with a 5, 15, 60 minute backoff the way quota walls expire.
How you notice it
account_paused in watch --actionable names the card and the login command to run. kanban stats lists logged-out accounts.

Jira sync is frozen =frozen

What changed
jira.py changed only in its docstring: “Frozen: bug fixes only; delete this module when the cake board stops using Jira.” (commit f22385d). The code is untouched. The README drops the web.jira_base_url step and the Jira bar of the web board.
Why
The commit gives the end condition: the module goes when the cake board stops using Jira.
How you notice it
Nothing changes at run time. Do not expect new Jira features; only bug fixes.

Prompt, agent and skill text ~changed

What changed
prompts/protocol.md and resume.md now use $TERMINALS and $RULES; new files are rules.md, terminals-work.md and terminals-review.md. Grants are no longer repeated in the prompt; kanban context lists them. kanban context adds pr and worktree to its header, skips [run] comments and drops the “Recent work” section. Smith and designer use kanban wait-ci, merge the base only when git merge-tree --write-tree shows a conflict or the base touched the PR's files, and write FOLLOW-UP: comments. Warden's partial review goes to the owner. The orchestrator skill gains numbered owner decisions, --touches, --merge-method and the setup skill's “Owner permissions” allow-list. skills/kanban-code-review/scripts/preflight.py ignores base merges (merge_only_since, :97), accepts a Gate sha that is an ancestor with only merges since, and reports a new INFO line “merge-only since APPROVED @ sha”. lint_on_edit.py pins ruff@0.16.10, and a test checks it matches runtime/uv.lock.
Why
Plan P2-6: the warden got smith's terminal list, which lacks request-changes; smith and designer shared about 600 words and the terminal verbs were explained three times. P2-3: [run] lines are 54 % of comments by count but about 7 % of bytes and pushed real comments out of the 30-comment window; “Recent work” was a flat 1.5 KB about other cards; grants appeared twice. P2-2: about 55 LPS smith sessions ran out of context, and every run opened with kanban context plus show --json, so the header now carries branch, base, PR and worktree. P0-2: the prompts told workers to sleep and to use gh pr checks --watch, and both fail (about 51 sessions); P1-3 replaced the recipe with wait-ci. P1-1: smith merged the base before every review, re-ran the gate and waited for CI again, with CI queues of 8 to 40 minutes. P0-7: about 20 review sessions where the warden had to explain away a “nonconventional commit” that was smith's own base merge. P2-5: merge-only re-reviews cost about 18 USD. P1-10: Denis wanted to set merge delegation once and get numbered per-PR decisions. P3-4: lint_on_edit.py ran uvx ruff with no version.
How you notice it
Shorter run prompts and a leaner kanban context. A re-review where only merges came after the approved sha is accepted and reported as merge-only.

Upgrade notes

Moving from dev7 to dev8

  1. Run the setup skill: /kanban-claude:setup. It takes an exclusive lock on upgrade.lock, backs up the database to $KANBAN_HOME/backups/ (five are kept), migrates schema 4 to 5, restarts the daemon with launchctl kickstart -k, waits up to 30 s for the new version to show in daemon.lock, and rewrites installed.json.
  2. Runs already in flight are not touched. New defaults apply to the next worker runs.
  3. Config keys gone: web.port, web.jira_base_url. New keys: effort.smith, effort.designer, effort.warden, effort.atlassian, budget.max_usd_per_card, budget.max_usd_per_board_day, notify.command, worker.plugin_allowlist, worker.mcp_allowlist.
  4. Verbs gone: kanban board and setup --port. Delete $KANBAN_HOME/web.secret if it exists.
  5. Switch the orchestrator's watch to kanban watch --actionable --wait --board <slug>, run as a background command.
  6. If a worker relied on one of your own plugins or MCP servers, add its name to worker.plugin_allowlist or worker.mcp_allowlist.
  7. A card that has already spent more than 15 USD blocks at its next claim. Raise budget.max_usd_per_card (0 turns the check off), then kanban unblock.

If setup stops with “the daemon still runs <ver>, not <ver>, after 30 s” or “nothing holds ... after 30 s”, run kanban doctor.

Rolling back to dev7 is manual and untested. Migration 5 first writes a copy of the schema 4 database to $KANBAN_HOME/backups/kanban-s4-<timestamp>-<hex>.db, and kanban doctor already tells you to restore the newest copy from that folder. To go back: stop the daemon, copy the newest kanban-s4-*.db over $KANBAN_HOME/kanban.db, then reinstall dev7. Work done after the upgrade is lost, and no test or run has checked these steps.

Range covered

The diff runs from d1a40cf to aff1750: the code at 9ff5306, the version bump, the merged pane rework and its docs. Walkthrough line numbers are at 9ff5306.

Board pane

The pane carries the board +added~changed✓fixed

What changed
hooks/board.tsx is rewritten (commits ce78ea9, f111d3b, 0d244be). A Needs you strip comes first: each question, grant, merge, login or quota wall with its reason and the command that answers it. A health line shows whether the daemon is live, whether dispatch is paused, and the last 24 hours' spend. Lanes list each card's priority, owner, age, and PR number or block kind; a selected card opens a detail view (branch, PR, last run, comments) that back or b leaves. A Recently merged section and one toast per new need follow. Inline from 72 columns the lanes sit side by side; a dock or anything narrower stacks them. To feed it, kanban --json digest adds each item's event id and reason, a paused field and daemon: {alive, version} read from daemon.lock, and kanban list adds block_kind (views.py, cli.py). The pane's $.state values are declared in types/index.d.ts, which plugin.json names under types.
Why
D4 made the pane the only visual view, so it has to show what the web board showed. The dev7 pane worked but was unstable and sparse. The stability fixes: the draw hook only reads $.state and starts no process; one refresh runs at a time, and a refresh started for a board that was unpinned meanwhile is dropped (a running hook keeps seeing $.state as it was when it started, so a module-level counter cancels it); a failed refresh keeps the last good read; the reopen key is per folder; ~/.local/bin/kanban is the fallback when PATH has no kanban; an older CLI without the new fields only hides the sections built on them.
How you notice it
After upgrading, run /kanban-board once in each folder where you want the pane back: the old global reopen key is deleted. A failed refresh shows “stale Ns” and the reason instead of an error screen. claude plugin test plugins/kanban-claude runs 19 pane tests.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Eight questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. A smith's Bash call has no explicit timeout and takes 7 minutes. What happens on dev8?

The runner sets BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 (runner.py:178); its comment says claude's 120 s default would cut off wait-ci. The 540 s limit belongs to wait-ci itself, not to Bash calls.

2. A card has spent 16.40 USD and the dispatcher claims it again. The default budget.max_usd_per_card is 15. What happens?

_over_budget runs inside claim. No run starts, and the cap is not checked mid-run (that is budget.max_usd_per_run). Raise the cap, then kanban unblock. If the claim was a review, the card unblocks back to review.

3. Warden approves a PR with the partial-review marker into a feature base. What does the daemon do?

store.complete sets owner_merge=1 and keeps the merge pending; run_due skips such rows. The children start once the sweep sees the PR merged. If the owner closes the PR unmerged, the card becomes merge_failed.

4. You run kanban watch --actionable --wait. New events arrive in this order: merged, review_requested, then blocked by worker:smith#3. When does the command exit?

--wait exits 0 once it has printed at least one line, and lines hidden by --actionable do not count (cli.py:520). Merged and review_requested are not actionable, so the blocked line is the first one printed.

5. You set notify.command today. The board already holds old blocked events, and then the daemon restarts. What does the command receive?

On its first pass the notify thread sets its cursor to the current highest event id, and it writes the cursor before it sends. A command that fails or times out (10 s) is logged and not retried.

6. How does setup know the restarted daemon is the new one?

wait_for_daemon(__version__) (install.py:297, called at :426) reads the JSON in daemon.lock. A dev7 daemon writes no version, so it reads as old. The web port is gone.

7. A smith runs kanban request-review on a branch that has two open PRs against the same base. What happens?

worker._find_pr refuses zero or several open PRs. With exactly one, it is used and the summary no longer needs a PR number.

8. wait-ci exits 2 three times and checks are still running. What does the agent text tell the smith to do?

If the third exit 2 says “no checks reported yet”, CI counts as passed and the summary says “no CI checks reported”. If checks are still running, the card blocks transient and retries by itself. That counts as a failed run, so dispatch.failure_limit (default 2) ends the retries as gave_up.

kanban-claude 0.2.0.dev8 release explainer. Source: github.com/DresvyanskiyDenis/claude-kanban-plugin

Built from the diff d1a40cf..aff1750 and the CHANGELOG.
